article_content: Announcement comes as the US confirms the first of its citizens able to leave Gaza via the Rafah crossing into Egypt. US Secretary of State Antony Blinken will travel to Israel and Jordan at the end of the week, the State Department has announced, as tensions remain high amid Israel’s escalating war against Hamas in Gaza. State Department spokesman Matthew Miller said on Wednesday that Blinken will begin his trip on Friday, his second to the region in less than a month, with a meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on the itinerary. He will reiterate US support for Israel’s right to defend itself, in accordance with international humanitarian law, and discuss the need to take all precautions to minimise civilian casualties, as well as our work to deliver humanitarian assistance, Miller told members of the press. The announcement comes as the US confirmed that some of its citizens were able to leave Gaza via the Rafah crossing into Egypt. Miller confirmed that an initial group of US citizens were among the foreigners who crossed into Egypt but did not provide a number. President Joe Biden said his administration would work to ensure that more US citizens would be able to leave Gaza in the coming days. Blinken’s planned visit comes as Israel steps up aerial bombardment of Gaza and slowly increases ground operations within the strip, where Israeli air raids and a restrictive siege have created dire humanitarian conditions. Jordan recalled its ambassador from Israel on Wednesday, stating that they would not return until Israel suspended its assault. Israel has rejected growing calls for a ceasefire and insists it is fighting to topple the Palestinian group Hamas, which launched a deadly attack on southern Israel on October 7, killing more than 1,400 people, mostly civilians, according to Israeli authorities. Rights groups, international organisations such as the UN, and neighbouring countries including Jordan have drawn attention to the devastating effect of Israel’s attacks and the harsh siege on the 2.3 million Palestinians in Gaza, where authorities have said 8,796 people have been killed, more than a third of them children. Arab countries condemned an Israeli attack on the densely populated Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza on Tuesday, which levelled an entire block of apartments and killed dozens of people, according to Palestinian authorities. Health services in Gaza have also been pushed to their limits or shuttered, as Israel’s siege chokes off access to necessities like fuel, electricity, and medical supplies. The US has frustrated Arab allies by backing Israel, even as officials temper statements of support with calls for abiding by international law, while rejecting calls for an end to the fighting. Asked about Jordan’s decision to withdraw its diplomat from Israel, Miller said that the US shares the concerns they expressed about the dire humanitarian situation in Gaza, but that reducing diplomatic channels is not productive.

Matthew Miller külügyi szóvivő szerdán elmondta, hogy Blinken pénteken kezdi meg útját, ami egy hónapon belül már a második látogatása a térségbe. Többek között találkozik Benjámin Netanjahu izraeli miniszterelnökkel. Kiemeli majd az Egyesült Államok támogatását Izrael jogos önvédelmi fellépése mellett, összhangban a nemzetközi humanitárius joggal, szó lesz a polgári áldozatok minimalizálásának fontosságáról, valamint a humanitárius segítségnyújtás megszervezéséről – mondta Miller újságíróknak. A közlemény akkor érkezik, amikor az Egyesült Államok megerősítette, hogy néhány állampolgára ki tudott jutni Gázából az egyiptomi Rafah-átkelőn keresztül. Miller szerint egy első csoport amerikai állampolgár is átlépett, de pontos számot nem közölt. Joe Biden elnök kijelentette, hogy kormánya mindent megtesz annak érdekében, hogy a következő napokban több amerikai állampolgár is elhagyhassa Gázát. Blinken tervezett látogatása arra az időszakra esik, amikor Izrael fokozza légi csapásait Gáza ellen, és lassan terjeszti ki szárazföldi műveleteit, miközben az izraeli légitámadások és a szigorú blokád miatt súlyos humanitárius válság alakult ki. Jordánia szerdán visszarendelte nagykövetét Izraelből, és közölte, hogy csak akkor küldi vissza, ha Izrael leállítja a támadásokat. Izrael elutasítja a tűzszüneti követeléseket, és azt állítja, hogy a palesztin Hamász szervezetet akarja felszámolni, amely október 7-én halálos támadást intézett Dél-Izrael ellen, több mint 1400 embert megölve, többségük civilt az izraeli hatóságok szerint. Jogvédő szervezetek, nemzetközi intézmények – köztük az ENSZ – és például Jordánia is felhívta a figyelmet arra, hogy az izraeli támadások és a szigorú blokád pusztító hatással van a 2,3 millió lakosú Gázára. A helyi hatóságok szerint 8796 embert öltek meg, akiknek több mint harmada gyermek. Az arab országok elítélték a Gáza északi részén található, sűrűn lakott Dzsabália menekülttábor keddi bombázását is, amely egy egész épületblokkot rombolt le, és a palesztin hatóságok szerint tucatnyi ember halálát okozta. Gázában az egészségügyi szolgáltatások szinte a végét járják vagy bezártak, mert Izrael blokádja megakadályozza a hozzáférést az alapvető erőforrásokhoz, például az üzemanyaghoz, az áramhoz és az orvosi eszközökhöz. Az Egyesült Államok csalódást okozott arab szövetségeseinek azzal, hogy kiáll Izrael mellett, miközben a tisztségviselők a nemzetközi jog betartását sürgetik, ugyanakkor elutasítják a harcok beszüntetésére felszólító kéréseket. Amikor a riporterek Jordánia döntéséről kérdezték, hogy visszahívja diplomatáját Izraelből, Miller azt mondta, hogy az Egyesült Államok megérti a Gázában kialakult súlyos humanitárius helyzettel kapcsolatos aggodalmakat, de a diplomáciai kapcsolatok meggyengítése nem célravezető.

article_content: If you are using a fake name on your Facebook account, maintaining a personal profile for your beloved pet, or have a second profile just for logging in to other sites, you could be one of the 83.09 million fake accounts Facebook wants to disable. In an updated regulatory filing released on Wednesday, the social media company said that 8.7 percent of its 955 million monthly active users worldwide are actually duplicate or false accounts. Joe Sullivan, Facebook’s chief security officer, stated: Our entire platform is based on people using their real identities. Facebook inspires status envy. So what are these 83 million undesired accounts doing? They are a mixture of innocent and malicious intentions, and Facebook divides them into three categories: duplicate accounts, misclassified accounts, and undesirable accounts. Duplicate accounts make up 4.8% (45.8 million) of Facebook’s total active member count. According to the network’s terms of service, users are not allowed to have more than one personal Facebook account or make accounts on behalf of other people. Parents creating Facebook accounts for their young children are violating two rules, since people under 13 are not allowed to have profiles. Misclassified accounts are personal profiles made for companies, groups, or pets. These 22.9 million accounts (2.4% of the total) are allowed on Facebook, but they need to be created as Pages. These accounts can be converted into approved Pages without losing information. Pets such as Boo, the self-anointed world’s cutest dog, are typically classified as Public Figures. The third group is the smallest, just 1.5% of all active accounts, but it is the most troublesome. There are 14.3 million undesirable accounts that Facebook believes have been created specifically for purposes that violate the company’s terms, such as spamming. We believe the percentage of accounts that are duplicate or false is meaningfully lower in developed markets such as the United States or Australia and higher in developing markets such as Indonesia and Turkey, the company said in the filing. The tallies were based on an internal sampling of accounts done by reviewers, and Facebook says the numbers may not represent the exact total. Facebook disables any false accounts it finds. While it removes all the information associated with the name from public view, it does not delete the account from its servers for safety and security reasons. The disabled account remains in a Facebook limbo, where the owner cannot access any content, not even by requesting a copy of the data, according to Facebook. If Facebook does shut down your account, the company states that you cannot create a new one without permission. Complete coverage: Facebook.

article_content: 'Kobe Bryant recorded his 20th career triple-double on Sunday as the Los Angeles Lakers edged the Toronto Raptors 129-122 in an overtime thriller. The five-time NBA champion tallied 31 points, 12 assists, and 11 rebounds, and was one of seven Lakers in double figures, including all five starters. Nick Young contributed 20 points off the bench, while Carlos Boozer netted 18, and Jordan Hill added 16 points and 12 rebounds.' 'Bryant's milestone performance took place at the Staples Center, helping the Lakers outlast the Raptors, whose 13-3 record entering the game was the best start in franchise history. Kyle Lowry posted 29 points, nine assists, and six rebounds for Toronto before fouling out late in overtime. Terrence Ross scored 20 points, and Lou Williams chipped in 19 off the bench.' 'In other NBA action, the San Antonio Spurs overcame the Boston Celtics 111-89, with Danny Green's 18 points helping to extend their winning streak to seven. Head coach Gregg Popovich returned from a two-game absence to guide the team through a four-game road trip. Meanwhile, the Chicago Bulls defeated the Brooklyn Nets 102-84, thanks in part to Jimmy Butler's 26 points and Pau Gasol's double-double of 25 points and 13 rebounds.' 'Elsewhere, the Golden State Warriors downed the Detroit Pistons 104-93 for their ninth straight victory, with Draymond Green scoring 20 points and Stephen Curry adding 16 points and 10 assists. The Memphis Grizzlies topped the Sacramento Kings 97-85, powered by Zach Randolph's 22 points and 12 rebounds, and Marc Gasol's 18 points. Dwyane Wade returned from injury to score 27, fueling the Miami Heat's 86-79 victory over the New York Knicks. The Orlando Magic edged the Phoenix Suns 93-90, and the Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves 107-93.' 'A triple-double occurs when a player reaches double digits in three statistical categories: points, rebounds, assists, steals, or blocks. Bryant's achievement adds another remarkable chapter to his illustrious career, underscoring his versatile impact on the game.'

article_content: London Mayor Boris Johnson criticized the government’s plans to screen passengers arriving from Ebola-hit countries, suggesting they make little sense and leave the public confused. Downing Street recently announced screening for air passengers from West Africa to prevent the deadly virus from entering the UK. Johnson, however, warned that a case of Ebola would likely appear in Britain eventually, most likely in London, and that preparations should be prioritized over ineffective screening announcements. Government plans have been inconsistent, with airlines uncertain about how screening will work to stop the virus, which has killed more than 4,000 people. The disease’s 21-day incubation period raises concerns that the screening measures might come too late. Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt is expected to detail the screening program soon. It is scheduled to begin by Tuesday or Wednesday, reflecting the U.S. timeline for its recent screening efforts. Earlier statements from the British government indicated that passenger screening would be impractical, but Number 10 later introduced enhanced measures at Heathrow, Gatwick, and Eurostar terminals for travelers from Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Guinea. This reversal has fueled public confusion. Johnson questioned the practicality of screening everyone, especially since early-stage Ebola carriers may not show a fever. He emphasized that exit checks are more crucial. The government’s sudden policy change comes after advice from the country’s Chief Medical Officer. Dr David Nabarro, the UN’s special envoy on Ebola, believes the virus could be under control within three months if international assistance continues. He notes that exit screening in the affected countries and strong community engagement are critical to slowing the epidemic. Meanwhile, the NHS has conducted preparedness drills. Johnson insists that the UK’s healthcare system is well-equipped, while others, like Labour’s Luciana Berger, call for clear communication rather than political finger-pointing.

Hozzátette, hogy az érintett országokban végzett kilépési ellenőrzések és a közösség bevonása kulcsfontosságú a járvány terjedésének lassításához. article_content: A New York woman named Sheri Astrachen is seeking major compensation from her millionaire husband, real estate executive Matthew Astrachen, after allegedly discovering his infidelity and losing access to their Long Island country club membership. She has filed a defamation lawsuit in Manhattan Supreme Court for $20 million, claiming he humiliated her by allowing her name to appear on the Old Westbury Golf & Country Club’s list of unpaid bills. According to court documents, this public listing made it seem as if she lacked the financial resources to cover membership costs. Matthew, who reportedly earns $4 million annually as a vice president at JLL (Jones Lang LaSalle Incorporated), has been married to Sheri for 18 years. They share three daughters. Sheri alleges she caught Matthew cheating with one or more saleswomen in New York City shops and subsequently asked him to leave their $4.7 million Old Westbury home. Though the couple filed for divorce last year, it has not yet been finalized. Sheri claims Matthew responded by not paying the country club bill and canceling some of her credit cards, which she calls economic and emotional warfare. Sheri insists she is entitled to maintain the luxurious lifestyle she enjoyed during the marriage, including expensive vehicles, annual vacations, housekeepers, and the country club membership. Matthew’s lawyer labeled the lawsuit as frivolous, indicating they plan to seek sanctions against Sheri’s legal counsel.

article_content: NEW YORK (CNN) – On Friday, the president of a group that promotes Times Square announced he will lobby the new mayor to regulate dozens of costumed characters, following the arrest of a man dressed as "Woody" from "Toy Story" on sex abuse charges. A 44-year-old man was charged Thursday with three counts of forcible touching and three counts of third-degree sex abuse, according to Detective Annette Markowski, a police spokeswoman. The alleged victims were two women, ages 21 and 22. Authorities say the abuse occurred around 8 p.m. Thursday at Broadway and West 46th Street. Tim Tompkins, president of the Times Square Alliance, commented that this case is the latest in a series of troubling incidents, underscoring the need for licensing and regulations. Tompkins plans to work with the mayor and City Council to develop an equitable and effective solution. He noted that many costumed characters in Times Square solicit tips from tourists, yet city officials have been cautious about imposing regulations due to First Amendment concerns. Times Square hosts a wide range of performers, from Muppet characters to the guitar-playing Naked Cowboy. While Tompkins says quirky entertainment is welcome, he stressed that creepy or illegal behavior should not be tolerated. Tompkins also mentioned previous discussions with former Mayor Michael Bloomberg's administration, although Bloomberg's term ended before any regulations were introduced. Tompkins has reached out to Mayor Bill de Blasio's office, but has yet to receive an official response. Critics argue that banning the costumed characters outright could violate freedom of expression. Tompkins believes that licensing them as a legitimate business would avoid such issues. These performers are not officially endorsed by intellectual property holders or the Times Square Alliance. Times Square was once known for high crime rates and adult entertainment venues, but it has experienced revitalization in recent decades, thanks to Broadway shows and vibrant attractions. A recent survey by the alliance estimates that 60 to 70 costumed individuals appear in Times Square during the peak summer season. This incident follows several others involving Times Square characters, including recent arrests of individuals dressed as "Cookie Monster," "Spider-Man," and "Super Mario" for alleged misconduct. In one case, a performer allegedly shoved a 2-year-old over a tip dispute; in another, a performer was charged with groping a woman.

Egy 44 éves férfit csütörtökön vádoltak meg három rendbeli erőszakos fogdosással és három rendbeli harmadfokú szexuális zaklatással, tájékoztatott Annette Markowski rendőrségi szóvivő. A feltételezett áldozatok két nő, 21 és 22 évesek. A hatóságok szerint a zaklatás csütörtök este 8 óra körül történt a Broadway és a 46. utca kereszteződésében. Tim Tompkins, a Times Square Alliance elnöke kiemelte, hogy ez az eset a legújabb a zavaró incidensek sorában, ami ráerősít arra, hogy szükség van az engedélyezési és szabályozási rendszerre. Tompkins azt tervezi, hogy együttműködik a polgármesterrel és a városi tanáccsal egy méltányos és hatékony megoldás kidolgozása érdekében. Megjegyezte, hogy számos jelmezes szereplő borravalót kér a turistáktól, de a város vezetése óvatos a szabályozással, mert ez sértheti az Első Alkotmánykiegészítés által biztosított jogokat. A Times Square olyan sokféle előadónak ad otthont, mint például a Muppet-figurák vagy a gitározó Naked Cowboy. Tompkins szerint a bohókás szórakoztatás elfogadható, de a hátborzongató vagy törvénytelen viselkedést nem szabad tolerálni. Tompkins megemlítette, hogy korábban már tárgyalt a korábbi polgármester, Michael Bloomberg adminisztrációjával, bár a ciklusa lejárt, mielőtt bármilyen szabályozást bevezettek volna. Tompkins megkereste Bill de Blasio polgármester irodáját is, de még nem kapott hivatalos választ. A kritikusok szerint a jelmezes szereplők teljes betiltása sértené a szabad véleménynyilvánítás jogát. Tompkins úgy véli, hogy ha üzleti tevékenységként engedélyezik őket, elkerülhetők lennének ezek a problémák. Ezeket az előadókat nem támogatják hivatalosan sem a szellemi tulajdonjogok tulajdonosai, sem a Times Square Alliance. A Times Square-t egykor magas bűnözési ráta és felnőtt tartalmú helyek jellemezték, de az elmúlt évtizedekben jelentős megújuláson ment át a Broadway-előadásoknak és a pezsgő látnivalóknak köszönhetően. A szövetség egyik friss felmérése szerint a nyári turistaszezon csúcsidőszakában 60-70 jelmezes ember jelenik meg a Times Square környékén. Ez az incidens több más, Times Square-i jelmezes karaktereket érintő esetet követ, beleértve a "Cookie Monster", "Spider-Man" és "Super Mario" jelmezét viselő előadók közelmúltbeli letartóztatásait. Egy esetben egy előadó állítólag meglökött egy kétéves gyereket, mert nem kapott borravalót; egy másikban pedig egy előadót azzal vádoltak, hogy megfogdosott egy nőt.
